# @zakkster/lite-worker

> Zero-GC per-frame Web Worker channel. Define a worker inline from a function,
> message it with transferable ArrayBuffers, and keep the main thread clean at
> 60fps. Zero dependencies, single file, full TypeScript types. It is NOT a
> Comlink-style RPC proxy: the point is a clean main thread for rendering while a
> simulation ticks off-thread, with nothing allocating in steady state. One
> worker = one extra core; cross-core parallelism is deferred to lite-worker-pool
> (v2.0.0). v1.1.0 adds frameChannel: a bounded, latest-wins frame channel over a
> fixed transfer pool, with lite-gl LAYOUT-compatible strides. v1.2.0 adds
> adoptCanvas: transferControlToOffscreen plus resize + visibility forwarding.

## Mental model

There is ONE Worker with TWO transports, discriminated on receipt by a single
`instanceof ArrayBuffer || ArrayBuffer.isView()` check (no allocation to route):

- raw (zero-GC hot path): the ArrayBuffer *is* the message, no envelope. Moved
  via transfer, never structured-cloned. Use for 60fps traffic (sim frames,
  audio sample blocks, pixel buffers).
- typed (control plane): `{t,i,d}` envelope. Use for init/config/request-response.
  `call()` allocates a Promise + a pending-map entry, so it is NOT for per-frame use.

## Core API (main thread)

- `defineWorker(moduleFn, options?) -> WorkerHandle`
  - `moduleFn(ctx)` is `.toString()`-serialized into a Blob URL. It MUST be
    self-contained: it cannot close over module scope and cannot use bare `import`.
  - `options`: `{ type?: "classic" | "module", name?: string, onError?: (e: Error) => void }`.
    Default `type` is `"classic"` (widest Blob-worker support).
  - The Worker is created lazily on `spawn()`. Also available as the default export.
- `WorkerHandle`:
  - `spawn(): this` — create the Worker. Idempotent while spawned; throws if destroyed.
  - `send(buffer, transfer?)` — raw transfer. When `transfer` is omitted the buffer
    is auto-transferred (it DETACHES on the sender). No-op before spawn / after terminate.
  - `onRaw(fn) -> off`, `offRaw(fn)` — raw buffers coming back from the worker.
  - `post(type, data?, transfer?)` — fire-and-forget typed message.
  - `call(type, data?, { transfer?, timeout? }?) -> Promise` — request/response.
    Rejects on handler throw, missing handler, timeout, or terminate. Allocates.
  - `on(type, fn) -> off`, `off(type, fn)` — typed pushes from the worker.
  - `terminate(): this` — stop the worker, reject pending calls; handle stays re-spawnable.
  - `destroy()` — idempotent full teardown; handle becomes unusable afterwards.
  - `spawned`, `destroyed` — booleans.

## Worker-side context (`ctx`)

Symmetric with the main side: `on(type, (data, reply?) => …)`, `off`, `onRaw`,
`offRaw`, `post`, `send`, `close()`. For a `call`, either invoke
`reply(data, transfer?)` OR return a value / resolving promise (auto-replies when
`reply` was not called). Throwing rejects the caller's promise.

## Ownership: the ping-pong

`send(buf)` transfers, so `buf` is detached afterward — you no longer own it. The
worker fills it and transfers it back to your `onRaw`. Hold TWO buffers and
ping-pong them (one in flight, one being drawn/consumed) to keep both threads busy
without allocating per frame.

## frameChannel (v1.1.0) — bounded, latest-wins frame passing

`frameChannel(transport, layout, options)`; also `handle.frameChannel(layout, options)`
and worker-side `ctx.frameChannel(layout, options)`. A fixed pool of pre-allocated
ArrayBuffers ping-pongs producer<->consumer via transfer: no per-frame data alloc,
no clone, memory bounded by the pool. If the consumer falls behind, intermediate
frames drop (latest-wins) instead of queueing.

- `transport`: a WorkerHandle or worker `ctx` — anything with `{ send, onRaw }`.
- `layout`: a Float32 stride number (needs `options.capacity`), `{ stride, capacity }`,
  or `{ bytes }`. The stride form matches lite-gl `LAYOUT` (POINT 8, QUAD/LINE 9): a
  channel of `{ stride, capacity }` holds a `Float32Array(capacity*stride)`, so a
  projected instance field crosses the boundary unmodified (same `i*stride` indexing).
- `options`: `{ role: "producer" | "consumer" (required), count?=2 (min 2, pool size),
  capacity?, onFrame? }`.
- Producer: `produce(fill) -> boolean` (fill(view, buffer); returns false when the
  pool is momentarily empty = frame dropped, sim just advances), `free`, `dispose()`.
- Consumer: `read() -> Float32Array | Uint8Array | null` (non-destructive, view cached
  until the next swap so it is allocation-free per rAF), `hasNew`, `dropped`, `dispose()`.
- Both expose `role`, `kind` ("f32"|"bytes"), `stride`, `capacity`, `byteLength`, `count`.
- Wire protocol: direction carries meaning (no tag/envelope) — a raw buffer at the
  consumer is a fresh frame; at the producer it is a recycle. So a frameChannel OWNS
  the raw `send`/`onRaw` stream: don't also use them directly while it is live. The
  typed `post`/`call`/`on` plane stays free for control.
- Allocation floor: data is transferred (zero copy) and envelope-free; the only
  hot-path cost is one typed-array header per buffer hop (transfer mints a new
  ArrayBuffer identity each hop, so views can't cross the boundary cached). `read()`
  itself allocates nothing. A SharedArrayBuffer-backed zero-header mode is planned
  for v1.2.0 (needs COOP/COEP).

## adoptCanvas (v1.2.0) — OffscreenCanvas with resize + visibility handled

`handle.adoptCanvas(canvasEl, options?)` (main) transfers the canvas to the worker
via transferControlToOffscreen and forwards the two things people forget: resize
(a ResizeObserver posts device-pixel w/h + dpr) and visibility (visibilitychange
posts pause/resume). Returns `{ resize(), pause(), resume(), dispose() }`. Throws
if the canvas lacks transferControlToOffscreen. `options`: `{ maxDpr?=2 }`.

`ctx.onCanvas(cb, options?)` (worker) receives it: `cb(canvas, ctl)` runs once with
the OffscreenCanvas and a control `ctl`:
- `ctl.canvas`, `ctl.width`, `ctl.height`, `ctl.dpr`, `ctl.visible`.
- `ctl.onResize((w, h, dpr) => …)` — fired after canvas.width/height is applied.
- `ctl.onVisibility((visible) => …)`.
- `ctl.frame(fn, { fps?, interval? })` — a render loop that prefers requestAnimationFrame
  (exposed on the worker global alongside OffscreenCanvas; vsync-paced), falling back
  to a timer when it's absent or when a rate is given. AUTO-PAUSES when the owning tab
  is hidden. `fn` gets a delta time (ms). Returns a stop fn.
- `ctl.pause()`, `ctl.resume()`, `ctl.dispose()`.

Uses reserved `lw:canvas*` typed message types (don't send those yourself). When
the worker both produces and draws, frames never cross back — no frameChannel is
involved; that is the point. frameChannel is for frames that must reach the main
thread or another worker; adoptCanvas is for when the worker owns the pixels.

## Constraints

- Self-contained body: no capture of surrounding scope, no bare `import`. Pass
  everything in via `post`/`send`, or inline it in the worker body.
- CSP: Blob workers need `worker-src blob:` (or `child-src blob:` on older policies).
- Transferables, not SharedArrayBuffer: the raw transport (and frameChannel, built
  on it) uses transfer semantics and needs NO cross-origin isolation (no COOP/COEP).
  Raw payloads must be an ArrayBuffer or an ArrayBuffer view. A SharedArrayBuffer
  frameChannel mode is planned for v1.2.0.
- No Blob URL leak: the object URL is revoked immediately after the Worker is
  constructed (the script is already fetched by then), so short-lived workers do
  not pile up object URLs. `destroy()` still frees the worker thread.

## Do / don't

- DO use `send`/`onRaw` for anything that runs every frame.
- DO use `post`/`call`/`on` for setup, configuration, and occasional RPC.
- DON'T use `call` inside a frame loop — it allocates.
- DON'T reference outer variables inside `moduleFn` — serialization drops them.
- DON'T reuse a buffer after `send()` — it has been transferred away.
- DO use `frameChannel` instead of hand-rolling the ping-pong for per-frame data;
  check `produce()`'s return (false = dropped) and drive `read()` from your rAF.
- DON'T mix direct `send`/`onRaw` with a live `frameChannel` on the same transport.

## Files

- Worker.js — single-file ESM source (exports `defineWorker`, `frameChannel`, default export, `WorkerHandle`; methods `handle.frameChannel`, `handle.adoptCanvas`; worker-side `ctx.frameChannel`, `ctx.onCanvas`).
- Worker.d.ts — full strict TypeScript declarations.
- demos/oscilloscope.html — off-thread waveform synthesis; tab 1 dogfoods `frameChannel` (worker produces, main draws, latest-wins), tab 2 dogfoods `adoptCanvas` (worker draws to a transferred canvas, main idle).
- bench/frame-soak.mjs — fast-producer/slow-consumer soak proving bounded memory + latest-wins (not shipped in the npm tarball).
